resting only on the three branches: cause, sign, medicine

hindi: अस्थान में विस्तार, आक्षेप और पुनरुक्ति आदि से रहित, और केवल हेतु, लिंग और औषध, इन तीन स्कंधों पर ही आधारित।
english: (It is) free from misplaced elaboration, objections, repetition and the like, and rests solely on the three branches (skandha): cause, sign and medicine.
notes: Subject (the work, saṃgrahaḥ of unit 26) is not in this unit. GROUPING: continues the sentence of unit 26 (the verse seems to run from unit 26 L2). ākṣepa can be 'digression' or 'objection'; asthāna-vistara is read 'elaboration out of place'. hetu, liṅga, auṣadha are the three skandhas as listed.

words.gloss: whose meaning and essence is deeply hidden
of the contradictions between its own and other treatises

hindi: प्रसंगों को प्रकाशित करने वाला, जिनका अर्थ और तत्त्व अत्यंत छिपा हुआ है, और अपने तथा दूसरे तंत्रों के विरोधों को अधिकतर दूर करने वाला।
english: (It is) the illuminator of passages whose meaning and essence are deeply hidden, and, for the most part, the remover of contradictions between its own and other treatises.
notes: Continues the description of the work (see unit 26/27). GROUPING: the sentence continues into unit 29 L1 (kariṣyate). 'svānyatantravirodha' could also be 'contradictions within one's own and other tantras'.

hindi: युग के अनुरूप प्रस्तुति विभाग करके की जाएगी। जो नित्य उपयोग में समझने में कठिन नहीं है, सभी अंगों में व्याप्त है और प्रकाशमान है।
english: A presentation suited to the age will be made, by divisions; (one that is) not hard to understand in daily use, pervading all the limbs, shining.

text_flags.why: possible: the genitive/ablative 'of the sun' has no construction; the neuter bhāsvat 'shining/like the sun' fits and the metre is unchanged.

notes: Line 2 is neuter and may qualify kāyacikitsitaṃ of unit 30 L1 ('where the treatment of the body ... is collected, easy in daily use ...'); GROUPING: possible link across the unit boundary. 'sarvāṅga' = all limbs (of the body or of the eight-limbed science); left literal. bhāsvataḥ is uncertain; the translation of the last words rests on the suggested bhāsvat.

hindi: जिसमें कायचिकित्सा का विशेष रूप से संग्रह किया गया है। यहाँ थोड़ा-सा भी कुछ आगम से रहित नहीं है।
english: Where the treatment of the body (kāyacikitsā) is collected in particular; here not the slightest thing is devoid of āgama (traditional authority).
notes: The printed 'mātrāmātra mapyatra' breaks mātrāmātram across two tokens (the m is in the second). The book Hindi reads 'nothing contrary to the āgama'; the Sanskrit says 'devoid of āgama'. Link to unit 29 L2 possible (see there).

hindi: वे विषय और ग्रंथ की वह रचना संक्षेप के लिए हैं; क्रम दूसरे प्रकार का है। संक्षेप में दोष तीन हैं: वायु, पित्त और कफ।
english: Those matters and that arrangement of the text are for the sake of brevity; the order is otherwise. In brief, the doṣas are three: Vāyu (Vāta), Pitta and Kapha.
notes: Line 1 is elliptical ('kramo'nyathā' = the order is different, i.e. from other works); the verb 'are' is supplied. Vāyu is the same as Vāta.

words.gloss: by the distinction of increase, decrease and equilibrium
by being high, middle and low

hindi: वे प्रत्येक वृद्धि, क्षय और साम्य के भेद से तीन प्रकार के हैं। वृद्धि और क्षय भी उत्कृष्ट, मध्य और अल्प होने से तीन-तीन प्रकार के हैं।
english: Each of them is threefold, by the distinction of increase, decrease and equilibrium; increase and decrease, too, are threefold, as high, middling and low.
notes: 'They' (te) are the three doṣas of unit 31.

words.gloss: having their seat below, in the middle and above

hindi: विकृत होने पर वे देह का नाश करते हैं और अविकृत रहने पर उसे बढ़ाते हैं। वे व्यापक होते हुए भी हृदय और नाभि के नीचे, मध्य में और ऊपर आश्रित रहते हैं।
english: Deranged, they destroy the body; unaltered, they make it grow. Though pervading (the body), they have their seats below, in the middle and above (the region of) the heart and navel.
notes: The printed 'vikṛtāvikṛtā' joins vikṛtāḥ and avikṛtāḥ (hiatus not kept). The two halves are read in parallel order (deranged: destroy; unaltered: make grow). The verse does not say which doṣa sits where; hṛnnābhyoḥ 'of heart and navel' is read as the reference points for below/middle/above.
lines_deva: विकृताविकृता देहं घ्नंति ते वर्द्धयंति च ॥
lines_iast: vikṛtāvikṛtā dehaṃ ghnaṃti te varddhayaṃti ca ||

words.gloss: of age, day, night and meal
reaching the end, middle and beginning

hindi: आयु, दिन, रात और भोजन के अंत, मध्य और आदि में वे क्रम से रहते हैं। उनसे अग्नि विषम, तीक्ष्ण और मंद होती है, और उनके सम होने पर सम होती है।
english: In the end, middle and beginning, in order, of age, day, night and meal they are present. Through them the digestive fire (agni) becomes irregular, sharp or slow, and when they are even it is even.
notes: The verse itself does not name which doṣa goes with end, middle, beginning, nor which with viṣama, tīkṣṇa, maṃda; the translation keeps the order only. 'ahorātri' read as ahaḥ + rātri. 'vayaḥ' = stage of life (age).

words.gloss: abiding in semen and menstrual blood

hindi: कोष्ठ क्रूर, मृदु या मध्यम होता है; उन दोषों के सम होने पर भी वह मध्यम होता है। जन्म के आरंभ में शुक्र और आर्तव में स्थित उन दोषों से, जैसे विष से विष के कीड़े का।
english: The koṣṭha (belly) is harsh, mild or medium; it is medium also when those (doṣas) are even. By those (doṣas) abiding in semen and menstrual blood at the beginning of birth, as by poison in the case of a poison-worm...
notes: GROUPING: the sentence is incomplete here; it continues in unit 36 L1 ('taiś ca ... prakṛtayaḥ'), so the true verse seems to be this L2 + next unit L1. The comparison 'viṣeṇeva viṣakṛmeḥ' is read as: as the nature of a poison-bred worm comes from poison (not stated in full). In the printed 'śukrārtavasthai rjanmādau' the r belongs to sthaiḥ (sandhi); koṣṭha is kept as 'belly, abdominal cavity'.
lines_deva: कोष्ठः क्रूरो मृदुर्मध्यो मध्यः स्यात्तैः समैरपि ॥
lines_iast: koṣṭhaḥ krūro mṛdurmadhyo madhyaḥ syāttaiḥ samairapi ||

hindi: और उन्हीं से तीन प्रकृतियाँ होती हैं, अलग-अलग हीन, मध्यम और उत्तम। समधातु वाली प्रकृति सबमें श्रेष्ठ है, और दो दोषों से उत्पन्न प्रकृतियाँ निंदनीय हैं।
english: And by them (there are) three (as printed; sapta, "seven", is suggested) constitutions (prakṛti), separately inferior, middling and best. The one with balanced dhātus is best among them all; those born of two doṣas are to be censured.

text_flags.why: possible: 'three' clashes with 'samastāsu' (among all) and with the next line, which brings in the balanced and two-doṣa types; seven constitutions fits the parallel known in the Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya. Same metre (2 syllables). Editors' note says the same.

notes: Translated as printed ('three'); the reading 'seven' is only suggested, so confidence is lowered. As printed, hīna-madhya-uttama (three grades) and 'three constitutions' coincide oddly. GROUPING: L1 completes the sentence begun in unit 35 L2.

uncertain.note: [src/split/hindi/eng] "तिस्रः प्रकृतयः" conflicts with next row (dual-doṣa types are included, 7 prakṛtis in Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya parallel) — suggested: तैश्च सप्त प्रकृतयो हीनमध्योत्तमाः पृथक्

hindi: उनमें अनिल रूक्ष, लघु, शीत, खर, सूक्ष्म और चल है। पित्त स्नेह से युक्त, तीक्ष्ण, उष्ण, लघु, विस्र, सर और द्रव है।
english: Among them, Anila (wind, Vāyu) is dry, light, cold, rough, subtle and moving. Pitta is oily, sharp, hot, light, rank-smelling, flowing and liquid.
notes: 'sasneha' is literally 'having oiliness'; some read it as 'slightly oily'. visra: raw-meat or fish-like smell, kept as 'rank-smelling'. 'rukṣa' is printed for rūkṣa (variant spelling).
lines_deva: तत्र रुक्षो लघुः शीतः खरः सूक्ष्मश्चलोऽनिलः ॥
पित्तं सस्नेहतीक्ष्णोष्णं लघु विस्रं सरं द्रवं ॥
lines_iast: tatra rukṣo laghuḥ śītaḥ kharaḥ sūkṣmaścalo'nilaḥ ||
pittaṃ sasnehatīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ laghu visraṃ saraṃ dravaṃ ||

words.gloss: from the decrease or aggravation of two or three of them

hindi: कफ स्निग्ध, शीत, गुरु, मंद, श्लक्ष्ण, मृत्स्न और स्थिर है। संसर्ग और सन्निपात उनमें से दो या तीन के क्षय या कोप से होते हैं।
english: Kapha is unctuous, cold, heavy, slow, smooth, clay-like and stable. Saṃsarga (combination) and sannipāta (conjunction) arise from the decrease or aggravation of two or three of them.
notes: mṛtsna: literally 'clayey'; commentators may explain it differently. The verb 'arise' is supplied; the order dvi-tri / saṃsarga-sannipāta is kept as printed.
lines_deva: स्निग्धः शीतो गुरुर्मंदः श्लक्ष्णो मृत्स्नः स्थिरः कफः ॥
lines_iast: snigdhaḥ śīto gururmaṃdaḥ ślakṣṇo mṛtsnaḥ sthiraḥ kaphaḥ ||

words.gloss: from the variation by excess and the like
rasa (fluid), blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen

hindi: वे दोनों उत्कर्ष आदि के भेदों से छह प्रकार के और दस प्रकार के कहे गए हैं। रस, असृक्, मांस, मेद, अस्थि, मज्जा और शुक्र ये धातुएँ हैं।
english: Those two are said to be sixfold and tenfold, through the variations of excess and the like. Rasa, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow and semen are the dhātus.
notes: 'Those two' = saṃsarga and sannipāta of unit 38. The count 'seven' appears only in the next unit (sapta). 'asṛj' = blood.

words.gloss: urine, faeces, sweat and the like
abiding in rasa and the others

hindi: सात दूष्य हैं, और मूत्र, शकृत्, स्वेद आदि मल भी हैं। जो रोग रस आदि में स्थित दोषों के होने पर उत्पन्न होते हैं,
english: Seven are dūṣyas (what can be vitiated), and so too are the malas (wastes): urine, faeces, sweat and the like. The diseases that arise when the doṣas abide in the rasa and the others...
notes: GROUPING: the relative clause 'ye' is completed in unit 41 L1 ('tān āhuḥ'); the true verse seems to be this L2 + next unit L1. 'sapta' is read as the seven dhātus of unit 39; the last pair is elliptical (malas also dūṣya, or malas in addition).

hindi: उन्हें उपचार से, यानी लाक्षणिक प्रयोग से, उनसे उत्पन्न कहा जाता है, जैसे घर-दाह (पाठ अनिश्चित)। प्रीणन, जीवन, लेप, स्नेह, धारण और पूरण,
english: They call them 'born of those' by figurative usage, like 'house-burning' (reading uncertain). Gratifying, sustaining life, coating, unctuousness, supporting and filling...

text_flags.why: possible: vṛta-dāha gives no clear sense; 'like house-burning' (a figure of speech) suits upacāra. Editors suggest the same.

notes: The simile is a doubtful restoration (low confidence); the Hindi/English of the book ('ring of fire') is not supported. GROUPING: L1 completes unit 40 L2; L2 begins a list continued in unit 42 L1 (karmāṇi dhātūnām), so the verse seems to be L2 + next unit L1.

uncertain.note: [src/hindi/eng] "वृतदाहवत्" probably "गृहदाहवत्" (like "house on fire", figurative usage); Hindi "जलते लोहे का गोला" is not supported by the Sanskrit and English "ring of fire" is a guess — suggested: तानाहुर्गृहदाहवत् ("as one says the house is burning")

hindi: और गर्भ की उत्पत्ति, ये धातुओं के कर्म क्रम से जाने जाते हैं। ये धातु और आहार सदा शरीर को धारण करते हैं।
english: ...and the generation of the embryo: they know (these) in order as the functions of the dhātus. The dhātus and foods always sustain the body.
notes: GROUPING: L1 finishes the list begun in unit 41 L2. The list items are nominative in apposition to karmāṇi; 'kramaśaḥ' = in order (the text pairs functions with dhātus in sequence, not spelled out here).

words.gloss: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, astringent

hindi: सबकी वृद्धि समान से होती है और विपरीत से उलटा होता है। रस हैं: स्वादु, अम्ल, लवण, तिक्त, ऊषण और कषाय।
english: For all (things), increase comes through what is alike, and the reverse through opposites. The tastes (rasa) are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent and astringent.
notes: 'sarveṣām' (of all) is left general (doṣas and dhātus are meant by context). ūṣaṇa 'pungent' (the taste usually called kaṭu).

hindi: ये छह द्रव्य के आश्रित हैं और पूर्व-पूर्व के क्रम से बल देने वाले हैं। उनमें से आदि के रस मारुत को नष्ट करते हैं, और तिक्त से आरंभ होने वाले तीन कफ को।
english: The six rest in a substance (dravya), and they bring strength in the order of precedence. Among them the first (three) destroy Māruta (wind), and the three beginning with bitter destroy Kapha.
notes: Printed ṣaḍ is ṣaṭ before d. 'yathāpūrvam' is read 'in order of precedence' (each earlier one more so); the Sanskrit does not spell out 'more'. 'ādyāḥ' has no number; 'the first three' follows from 'trayaḥ' in the second half and the six tastes of unit 43. ghnanti is literally 'strike down'.

hindi: कषाय, तिक्त और मधुर पित्त को नष्ट करते हैं, परंतु दूसरे उसे उत्पन्न करते हैं। द्रव्य तीन प्रकार का है: शमन, कोपन और स्वस्थ के लिए हितकर।
english: Astringent, bitter and sweet (destroy) Pitta, but the others make Pitta. A substance is thus threefold: pacifying, provoking, and good for the healthy.
notes: The verb of the first clause (ghnanti) is carried over from unit 44 L2. 'kurvate' with pittam is literally 'make'; read as 'produce / provoke'. The Sanskrit of the verse itself speaks only of the rasas, as in the text.

words.gloss: from the predominance of the hot or cold quality
having the nature of sweet, sour or pungent

hindi: उष्ण और शीत गुण की प्रधानता से उनमें वीर्य दो प्रकार का माना गया है। द्रव्य का विपाक तीन प्रकार का है, स्वादु, अम्ल या कटुक स्वभाव वाला।
english: Among these, vīrya (potency) is held to be twofold, from the predominance of the hot or cold quality. The vipāka (ripening, final transformation) of a substance is threefold, having the nature of sweet, sour or pungent.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kaduka' is not a word; kaṭuka 'pungent' fits and completes the list of three; the Devanagari also shows द for ट.

notes: vīrya and vipāka are kept with a short gloss only.

words.gloss: heavy, slow, cold, unctuous, smooth, dense, soft, stable

hindi: गुरु, मंद, हिम, स्निग्ध, श्लक्ष्ण, सांद्र, मृदु और स्थिर, ये गुण हैं; सूक्ष्म और विशद सहित तथा अपने विपरीतों सहित वे बीस हैं।
english: Heavy, slow, cold, unctuous, smooth, dense, soft and stable: these are the qualities; with subtle and clear added, and with their opposites, they are twenty.
notes: Count: the eight listed plus sūkṣma and viśada make ten; with opposites, twenty. 'hima' (snow, cold) is kept as 'cold'.

hindi: इंद्रियों के विषय, व्यवायी और विकासी, ये अन्य गुण हैं। व्यवायी पूरे शरीर में फैलकर पाक के योग्य होता है।
english: The objects of the senses, vyavāyin and vikāsin are the other qualities. The vyavāyin (quality), having pervaded the whole body, is fit for (leads to) pāka (ripening, cooking).

text_flags.why: possible: printed with ṣ; the known quality is vikāsin (vi-√kas 'expand'), but in this scan ś is often printed as ṣ, so vikāśī (vi-√kaś) is equally possible; the same spelling recurs in unit 49

notes: pākāya kalpate is literally 'is fit for ripening'; left plain. vyavāyin and vikāsin are kept untranslated with a short gloss.
lines_deva: इंद्रियार्था व्यवायी च विकाषी चापरे गुणाः ॥
lines_iast: iṃdriyārthā vyavāyī ca vikāṣī cāpare guṇāḥ ||

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (as printed; 'tau' du. suggested)

hindi: विकासी फैलते हुए ही संधियों के बंधनों को ढीला कर देता है। परंतु कुछ लोगों ने तीक्ष्ण और प्रकर्ष की कल्पना की है।
english: The vikāsin (quality), merely by expanding, loosens the bonds of the joints. But by some, sharpness (tīkṣṇa) and excess (prakarṣa) are posited (as further qualities).

text_flags.why: possible: ṣ for s or ś, as in unit 48
possible: √kas or √kaś 'expand' rather than √kaṣ; same spelling issue
possible: 'sas' is unexplained; the metre stays unsettled (satīkṣṇa has the same syllable count as sastīkṣṇa, tīkṣṇaprakarṣau would give 14); the editors flag it
possible: 'sau' (that) has no clear role; 'tau' (those two) would fit with parikalpitau.

notes: Second line is damaged (editors' note); the words sa and sau are unresolved, so only the plain sense 'some posit tīkṣṇa and prakarṣa' is given, with 'as further qualities' supplied from context. Do not rely on it.

uncertain.note: [src] "सस्तीक्ष्णप्रकर्षौ तु कैश्चित्सौ" unclear (स/सौ) — suggested: सतीक्ष्णप्रकर्षौ तु कैश्चित्...

hindi: सत्त्व, रज और तम, ये तीन महागुण कहे गए हैं। काल, अर्थ और कर्मों का योग, हीन, मिथ्या या अतिमात्र,
english: Sattva, rajas and tamas: these three are called the great qualities (mahāguṇa). The conjunction of time, objects and actions, whether deficient, wrong or excessive...
notes: Printed 'satvaṃ' is a variant spelling of sattvam (not flagged as an error). The second sentence has no predicate in this unit (it continues in the next).

words.gloss: sole cause of disease and health

hindi: और सम्यक् योग को रोग तथा आरोग्य का एकमात्र कारण जानना चाहिए। दोषों की विषमता रोग है और दोषों की समता अरोगता, अर्थात् रोग का न होना है।
english: And right combination (samyag-yoga) is to be known as the one cause of both disease and health. Disease is imbalance of the doṣas; freedom from disease is balance of the doṣas.
notes: The sentence opens with ca, so it continues from the preceding verse (outside this unit); the unit alone does not say what is combined. rogārogyaikakāraṇam is taken as 'sole cause of disease and health'.

words.gloss: by the division into inner and outer
words.gram: m. inst. sg., dvandva and tat-puruṣa

words.gloss: from the difference of body and mind

hindi: निज और आगन्तु के विभाग से रोग दो प्रकार के माने गए हैं। शरीर और मन के भेद से उनका अधिष्ठान, अर्थात् आधार, भी दो प्रकार का है।
english: Diseases are held to be of two kinds, by the division into nija (one's own, arising within) and āgantu (coming from outside). Their seat (adhiṣṭhāna) is also twofold, by the difference of body and mind.
notes: nija and āgantu are glossed literally ('one's own', 'arriving'); the text gives no further definition here.

hindi: मन के दो दोष रज और तम कहे गए हैं। दर्शन, स्पर्शन और प्रश्न के द्वारा रोगी की परीक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: Rajas and tamas are declared to be the two doṣas of the mind. One should examine the patient by looking, touching and questioning.
notes: The first ca after tamaḥ joins rajas and tamas; the second ca (dvau ca) is a connective. Two unrelated statements are joined in one unit, but each is complete.

words.gloss: by cause, early sign, sign, upaśaya and āpti
by the difference of land and body

hindi: रोग की परीक्षा निदान, प्राग्रूप, लक्षण, उपशय और आप्ति से करनी चाहिए। यहाँ भूमि और देह के भेद से देश को दो प्रकार का कहते हैं।
english: The disease is to be examined by its cause (nidāna), early sign (prāgrūpa), characteristic sign (lakṣaṇa), upaśaya and āpti. Here they speak of locality (deśa) as twofold, by the difference of land and body.
notes: The verb of line 1 is not in the unit; it is carried over from parīkṣeta in the previous unit, and rogam is taken as its object. upaśaya (literally 'what settles, what is found suitable') and āpti (literally 'attainment') are kept as printed; the text here does not define them. iha could also be 'in this world/science'.

hindi: भूमि के देश को तीन प्रकार का बताना चाहिए: जांगल, जिसमें वात की प्रधानता है; अनूप, जिसमें कफ की अधिकता है; और साधारण, जिसमें मल सम हैं।
english: One should designate the land-region as threefold: jāṅgala, in which vāta predominates; anūpa, in which kapha is abundant; and sādhāraṇa ('common'), in which the mala are equal.
notes: The three region names are kept as printed. sama-mala is read as 'equal mala', mala here presumably meaning the doṣas (not stated in the unit).

words.gloss: moments and so on, and stage of disease
bringing about the use of medicine

hindi: क्षण आदि और रोग की अवस्था, यह काल है, जो औषध के प्रयोग को सम्पन्न करता है। संक्षेप में औषध दो प्रकार की है: शोधन और शमन।
english: Time, which brings about the application of medicine, is moments and so on and the stage of the disease. In brief, medicine is twofold: śodhana (purifying) and śamana (pacifying).
notes: The printed compound kṣaṇādivyādhyavasthā is read as one dvandva; it could also be kṣaṇādiḥ (nom. sg.) + vyādhyavasthā with a lost visarga (kṣaṇādirvyādhyavasthā); the sense is the same and the line has 16 syllables either way. 'ca' after it is then a connective.

words.gloss: of those born in the body

hindi: शरीर में उत्पन्न होने वाले दोषों की क्रम से परम औषध बस्ति, विरेक और वमन हैं, तथा तेल, घी और मधु।
english: For the doṣas born in the body, in order, the supreme remedies are basti, purgation and emesis, and likewise oil, ghee and honey.
notes: The doṣas are not named in the unit, so 'in order' (krameṇa) is left open as to which remedy goes with which doṣa; the verse does not say so. Whether krameṇa governs the second triad (oil, ghee, honey) is likewise not stated.
lines_deva: बस्तिर्विरेको वमनं तथा तैलं घृतं मधु ॥
lines_iast: bastirvireko vamanaṃ tathā tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu ||

words.gloss: intellect, steadiness, knowledge of the self and so on
words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva and tat-puruṣa

words.gloss: remedy for the doṣas of the mind

hindi: बुद्धि, धैर्य और आत्मा आदि का ज्ञान मन के दोषों की श्रेष्ठ औषध है। अब आगे इस तन्त्र के अध्यायों का संग्रह कहा जाएगा।
english: Intellect, steadiness and knowledge of the self and so on are the supreme remedy for the doṣas of the mind. Next, the summary of the chapters of this treatise will be stated.
notes: dhīdhairyātmādivijñānam can also be read 'knowledge of dhī, dhairya, ātman and so on'; the sense is close. param ca ataḥ is taken as 'and further, from here'.

words.gloss: chapters: Āyuṣkāmīya (as printed āyuṣya-), the student's purpose, day, season, non-arising of disease

hindi: आयुष्यकामीय (छपा पाठ; सम्भवतः आयुष्कामीय), शिष्य का प्रयोजन, दिन, ऋतु और रोगों का न होना; द्रव और अन्न का ज्ञान, संरक्षा, विरुद्ध, अज्ञान (पाठ संदिग्ध), भोज और पानसम्बन्धी अध्याय।
english: The chapters on: the desire for life (printed āyuṣya-kāmīya; probably Āyuṣkāmīya), the student's purpose, the day, the season, and the non-arising of disease; knowledge of liquids and of food, protection, the incompatible, ajñāna ('ignorance'; reading doubtful, see text_flags), eating and drinking.

text_flags.why: possible: the colophon in unit 75 reads āyuṣkāmīya; here -ya- may be a printing or reading slip
possible: ajñāna (ignorance) is an odd chapter heading; the book's Hindi reads viruddha-anna but also ajñāna-bhoja, so the emendation is a guess

notes: This is a list of chapter titles of the first sthāna, with no verb; the unit is translated as a list. The meaning of śiṣyārtha, asambhava (read 'non-arising') and of -pānikāḥ is uncertain, and the second line is only partly interpretable. Line 2 also has a stray space (dravānnajñāna saṃrakṣā...); the two parts may be one compound.

words.gloss: measure of what is eaten, knowledge of medicines, the best, purification and so on, compilations
great decoctions, various substances and so on, distinctions of taste

hindi: खाए हुए (भोजन) की मात्रा, औषधों का ज्ञान, श्रेष्ठ, शुद्धि आदि और संग्रह; महान कषाय, अनेक द्रव्य आदि और रसों के भेद करने वाले अध्याय।
english: The chapters on: the measure of what is eaten, knowledge of medicines, the best (śreṣṭha), purification and so on, and compilations; the great decoctions (mahākaṣāya), various substances and so on, and the distinctions of taste (rasa).

notes: A list of chapter titles without a verb. How the items group into chapters (e.g. 'śreṣṭha' and 'saṃgraha') is not clear from the Sanskrit alone, so the rendering is literal. -bhedakāḥ is taken as 'distinguishing'.

words.gloss: knowledge of doṣas etc., tad-veda (printed; perhaps tad-bheda 'their divisions'), their management, disease, medicine
treatment, oiling, sweating, purification, āsthāpana, nāvana

hindi: दोष आदि का विज्ञान, तद्वेद (छपा पाठ; सम्भवतः तद्भेद, अर्थात् उनके भेद), उनकी क्रिया, रोग और भेषज; चिकित्सा, स्नेह, स्वेद, शुद्धि, आस्थापन और नावन।
english: Knowledge of the doṣas and so on, tad-veda (printed; perhaps tad-bheda, 'their divisions'), their management, disease and medicine; treatment (cikitsā), oiling (sneha), sweating (sveda), purification, āsthāpana and nāvana.

hindi: ये चालीस अध्याय सूत्र हैं। शारीर कहा जाता है: पुत्र के लिए, गर्भ का अवतरण, आचरण, विपत्ति और शरीर से उत्पन्न होने वाले अध्याय।
english: These forty chapters are the Sūtra (section). The Śārīra is spoken of: the chapters on the aim of a son, the descent of the embryo, conduct, mishaps, and the body-born.
notes: GROUPING: the sentence runs on into unit 64 (the list of Śārīra chapter titles continues there, ending with sadūtā dvādaśādhyāyā), so units 63 and 64 belong together. words.gloss: veins, vital spots, constitution, account, deformed, limb, movement, diseases

hindi: सिरा, मर्म, प्रकृति का आख्यान, विकृत अंग, तथा ईहित-आमय (चेष्टा और रोग, यह पाठ संदिग्ध); दूत सहित बारह अध्याय हैं। सब रोगों से सम्बन्धित निदान।
english: Veins (sirā), vital spots (marma), the account of constitution (prakṛti), deformed limbs, and 'īhita-āmayāḥ' (read here as movements and diseases, but doubtful); with the messenger chapter there are twelve chapters. The Nidāna, concerning all diseases.

words.gloss: of fever, blood, breath, yakṣma and so on, intoxication and so on, arśas, and those with atisāra
of urine-obstruction and the prameha group
of abscess and so on, and of the abdomen

hindi: ज्वर, रक्त, श्वास, यक्ष्मा आदि, मद आदि, अर्श और अतिसार वालों के; मूत्राघात और प्रमेहों के; विद्रधि आदि के और उदर के भी।
english: Of fever, blood, breath, yakṣma and so on, intoxication and so on, arśas and those with atisāra; of urinary obstruction and the pramehas; of vidradhi and so on, and of the abdomen.
notes: A genitive list of subjects of the Nidāna chapters (see 64: nidānaṃ sārvarogikam), whose number 'ṣoḍaśa' appears in unit 66. No verb. asṛk (literally 'blood') and śvasa (literally 'breathing') are kept literal; disease names (yakṣma, arśas, atisāra, prameha, vidradhi) are given as terms, not modern diagnoses. The compound's final -ām covers all members; the exact grouping of members is uncertain.

words.gloss: of pāṇḍu, kuṣṭha and those afflicted by wind

hindi: पाण्डु, कुष्ठ, वात से पीड़ित और वातास्र के, ये सोलह; तथा ज्वर, रक्त और कास, श्वास और यक्ष्मा की चिकित्सा।
english: Of pāṇḍu, kuṣṭha, those afflicted by wind (anila) and vātāsra: sixteen. And the treatment (cikitsā) of fever, of blood and cough, and of breath (śvāsa) and yakṣma.

words.gloss: in all eye, eye-throbbing and eye-pāka
in the ear, nose and mouth

hindi: समस्त नेत्र, नेत्र की फड़कन और नेत्र के पाक में; कान, नाक और मुख में; सिर में, व्रण में, इसी प्रकार दो-दो; सद्यः भंग में और भगन्दर में।
english: In the whole of the eye, in eye-throbbing and eye-pāka; in the ear, nose and mouth; in the head, in the wound (vraṇa), likewise two each; in sudden breaking and in bhagandara.
notes: Title list with no verb. sarvadṛkspandadṛkpāke is read as 'all (diseases of the) eye, eye-throbbing, eye-pāka' (pāka literally 'ripening'); the grouping within the compound is uncertain. 'dvau dvau' (two each) may apply to some or all of the items in line 2; the verse does not say which.
lines_deva: मूर्ध्नि व्रणे तथा द्वौ द्वौ सद्योभंगे भगंदरे ॥
lines_iast: mūrdhni vraṇe tathā dvau dvau sadyobhaṃge bhagaṃdare ||

words.gloss: in diseases of the hidden parts

hindi: ग्रन्थि आदि में, छोटे रोगों में, गुह्य रोग में अलग-अलग दो; विष में दो, साँप और कीट में दो, और मकड़ियों और चूहे में।
english: In granthi and so on, in minor diseases, and in diseases of the hidden parts, a pair separately; in poison, two; in the snake and the insect, two; and in spiders and the rat (or: in the snake and insect, then two for spiders and the rat).
notes: Title list with no verb. In line 2 no number is given for 'lūtāsu mūṣake' (spiders, rat); it may share the 'two' of the preceding pair. pṛthak dvayam is read 'a pair for each, separately'. guhya-roga is literally 'disease of hidden (parts)'. Alternative grouping (the book's own Hindi/English): viṣe dvau | bhujage kīṭe | dvau ca lūtāsu mūṣake, i.e. 'two' for spiders and the rat; the draft attaches 'dvau ca' to bhujage kīṭe. The word order allows both.
lines_deva: विषे द्वौ भुजगे कीटे द्वौ च लूतासु मूषके ॥
lines_iast: viṣe dvau bhujage kīṭe dvau ca lūtāsu mūṣake ||

hindi: विष में, विष के उपयोग में, और इसी प्रकार रसायन पर एक अध्याय; वाजीकरण को लक्ष्य करके पचासवाँ अध्याय, जो अंगों को पूर्ण करने वाला है (पाठ संदिग्ध)।
english: In poison, in the use of poison, and likewise a chapter on rasāyana; aiming at vājīkaraṇa, the fiftieth, adhyāṃga-pūraṇa (printed; read as 'the chapter that completes the limbs', doubtful).

text_flags.why: possible: adhyāṃga for adhyāyāṅga (adhyāya + aṅga); the editors suggest adhyāyaḥ aṅga-pūraṇaḥ

notes: Title list. The meaning of aṅga-pūraṇa is uncertain: 'completing the limbs' is a literal rendering, and 'limbs' is not specified. pañcāśaḥ is read as the ordinal 'fiftieth'. Which chapter vājīkaraṇam uddiśya refers to is not clear beyond the grammar.

uncertain.note: [split] "अध्यांग पूरणः" — suggested: अध्यायः अंग पूरणः (?)

hindi: एक सौ पचास अध्याय छह स्थानों द्वारा कहे गए हैं। इस प्रकार आयुष्कामीय नामक प्रथम अध्याय।
english: One hundred and fifty chapters are declared in six sections. Thus the first chapter, named Āyuṣkāmīya.
notes: Unit 59 prints the same title as āyuṣyakāmīya (flagged there). 'pañcāśad adhyāyaśatam' is read as fifty plus a hundred (150 in all); the order is unusual but the sum is the natural reading. Line 2 is the closing colophon of chapter 1; 'iti ... nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ || 1 ||'.

uncertain.note: [src/hindi] colophon spells आयुष्कामीय but row 13 and Hindi use आयुष्यकामीय — suggested: uniform spelling आयुष्कामीय or आयुष्यकामीय
